title: Apply and peel a cold-wax strip
instruction: Apply the wax strip to the top of the silicone leg form, smooth it while keeping the dry edge available, then peel it back in one quick pull. Leave the strip clear of the leg and release it.
context: This is the application-and-removal movement used with a cold-wax strip, practised on a rigid silicone leg form. It does not test hair removal or treatment on a person.
setup: A rigid silicone leg form is a horizontal cylinder 340 mm long and 120 mm in diameter, supported on a 65 x 350 x 15 mm plastic rest. A flexible 45 x 160 mm yellow nonwoven cold-wax training strip lies flat on the table beside it, with a marked dry edge at one end. The strip has a tacky underside and approximately 1 mm total thickness. Both hands start open. All dimensions and the single starting layout are shown in the setup photograph and scene code.
scoring: 0.25 for smoothing at least 70% of the strip flat against the form while holding its marked dry edge. 0.5 if it is then completely removed and left clear of the form, released for two seconds. 1.0 if the removal takes at most two seconds, measured from the held edge moving 2 cm until the last adhesive contact releases. Pull back close to the form: raising the held end more than 7 cm above a remaining bond at a steeper-than-55-degree pull, tearing or overstretching the strip earns 0. Outcomes that do not meet an application milestone score 0. Use video, a ruler and a stopwatch.
fidelity: Native arms and rigid silicone form. A coarse flexible sheet models gravity, stretch, shear, bending and form contact. Tacky contact creates bonds; finger pads smooth the sheet and local tension releases a peel front. Closing-finger grasps are idealized. Hair, skin deformation and wax chemistry are omitted. This measures strip handling on a practice form, not hair removal or skin safety.
reset_notes: Use a fresh strip and restore it to the flat starting position. Reset the arms; the leg form stays fixed.
